claim: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a classification statement.

claim: CDV causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with reference to recent reports.

claim: CDV vaccines are highly effective.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) belongs to morbillivirus, including measles virus (MeV) and rinderpest virus, which causes serious immunological and neurological disorders in carnivores, including dogs and rhesus monkeys, as recently reported, but their vaccines are highly effective.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: The attachment glycoprotein hemagglutinin (CDV-H) at the CDV surface utilizes signaling lymphocyte activation molecule (SLAM) and Nectin-4 as entry receptors.
source: The attachment glycoprotein hemagglutinin (CDV-H) at the CDV surface utilizes signaling lymphocyte activation molecule (SLAM) and Nectin-4 (also called poliovirus-receptor-like-4; PVRL4) as entry receptors.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: The crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain was determined at 3.2 Å resolution.
source: Here, we determined the crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain at 3.2 Å resolution, revealing that CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by crystallographic data in Table 2.

claim: CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
source: Here, we determined the crystal structure of the globular head domain of CDV-H vaccine strain at 3.2 Å resolution, revealing that CDV-H exhibits a highly tilted homodimeric form with a six-bladed β-propeller fold.
evidence: This is a primary structural finding stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H.
source: While the predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H, that of SLAM is similar but partially different, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison in Figure 5.

claim: The SLAM-binding site of CDV-H is similar but partially different from that of MeV-H, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
source: While the predicted Nectin-4-binding site is well conserved with that of MeV-H, that of SLAM is similar but partially different, which is expected to contribute to host specificity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison in Figure 4.

claim: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only.
source: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only, supporting the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The glycan shield of CDV-H supports the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
source: Five N-linked sugars covered a broad area of the CDV-H surface to expose receptor-binding sites only, supporting the effective production of neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an interpretation of the glycosylation pattern.

claim: The glycan shield features are common to MeV-H, although the glycosylation sites are completely different.
source: These features are common to MeV-H, although the glycosylation sites are completely different.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 6.

claim: High-speed atomic force microscopy revealed highly mobile features of the CDV-H dimeric head via the connector region.
source: Furthermore, real-time observation using high-speed atomic force microscopy revealed highly mobile features of the CDV-H dimeric head via the connector region.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by HS-AFM data in Figure 7.

claim: Sugar-shielded tilted homodimeric structure and dynamic conformational changes are common characteristics of morbilliviruses.
source: These results suggest that sugar-shielded tilted homodimeric structure and dynamic conformational changes are common characteristics of morbilliviruses and ensure effective fusion entry and vaccination.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the structural and dynamic findings.

claim: CDV infects dogs as well as other carnivores.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) infects dogs as well as other carnivores, and causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency (Appel and Summers, 1995; An et al., 2008; von Messling et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CDV causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency.
source: Canine distemper virus (CDV) infects dogs as well as other carnivores, and causes acute, highly contagious, febrile diseases that affect the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and central nervous systems, along with serious temporary immunodeficiency (Appel and Summers, 1995; An et al., 2008; von Messling et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In 2008, the Chinese group reported a natural infection of CDV in rhesus monkeys.

claim: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome.
source: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome that is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae, to which the measles virus (MeV) also belongs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a classification statement.

claim: CDV is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae.
source: CDV is an enveloped virus with a non-segmented, negative-strand RNA genome that is classified in the genus Morbillivirus of the family Paramyxoviridae, to which the measles virus (MeV) also belongs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a classification statement.

claim: SLAM is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets.
source: SLAM, which has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region, is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets, reflecting the tropism and immunosuppressive nature of CDV (Yanagi et al., 2009; Schwartzberg et al., 2009; Kiel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SLAM has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region.
source: SLAM, which has two immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains in the extracellular region, is expressed on thymocytes, activated lymphocytes, mature dendritic cells, macrophages, and platelets, reflecting the tropism and immunosuppressive nature of CDV (Yanagi et al., 2009; Schwartzberg et al., 2009; Kiel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The host species of CDV is partly determined by their SLAMs.

claim: CDV-H binds to dog Nectin-4 with low affinity (Kd ~ 10−7 to 10−6 M) and fast kinetics.

claim: The binding characteristics of the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction were similar to those of CDV-H–SLAM.
source: The binding characteristics of the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction were similar to those of CDV-H–SLAM, which is typical for receptor recognition of viral attachment proteins.

claim: CDV-H exhibits a sufficient response to hNectin-4 with similar binding kinetics to the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction.
source: SPR experiments clearly demonstrated that CDV-H exhibits a sufficient response to hNectin-4 with similar binding kinetics to the CDV-H–dNectin-4 interaction, as shown in Figure 1D and Table 1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by SPR data in Figure 1D and Table 1.

claim: The molecular weight of the non-reducing soluble CDV-H determined by gel filtration chromatography and SDS–PAGE matched its dimer form.
source: The molecular weight of the non-reducing soluble CDV-H determined by gel filtration chromatography and sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS–PAGE) matched its dimer form (Figure 1B), indicating that the head domain of CDV-H exists as a disulfide-linked homodimer.

claim: The head domain of CDV-H exists as a disulfide-linked homodimer.

claim: MeV-H shares approximately 30% sequence identity in the head domain with CDV-H.

claim: The head domains of CDV-H of vaccine strain exhibit a six-bladed β-propeller structure, which is essentially the same as recent cryo-EM structure of wild-type CDV-H ectodomain (r.m.s.d. = 0.584–0.743 Å).

claim: The homodimer orientation of CDV-H is similar to the MeV-H homodimer structures and distinct from other paramyxoviruses, such as parainfluenza virus 5.

claim: All 20 interacting residues of hNectin-4 were identical to dNectin-4.

claim: The crystal structure of CDV-H shows a connector domain (residues 158–187) that mediates a head domain to the stalk region.

claim: The CDV-H dimer was observed as two globules clustered together in most cases, but sometimes, each domain moved independently.

claim: CDV-H could adopt both associated and dissociated forms.

claim: The distribution of distances between each head domain in the CDV-H dimers showed approximately 15 nm as a major peak.

claim: X-ray diffraction datasets were collected on NW-12 beamline at the Photon Factory (Tsukuba) and BL-41XU at Spring-8 (Harima).
source: X-ray diffraction datasets were collected on NW-12 beamline at the Photon Factory (Tsukuba) and BL-41XU at Spring-8 (Harima) and integrated and scaled using HKL2000 (HKL Research, Inc) (Minor et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: The molecular replacement software, MOLREP, using the crystal structure of MeV-H (PDB ID code: 2Z6B) as a search model, provided a clear solution.
source: The molecular replacement software, MOLREP, using the crystal structure of MeV-H (PDB ID code: 2Z6B) as a search model, provided a clear solution (Hashiguchi et al., 2007; Vagin and Teplyakov, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Model refinement calculations were executed using REFMAC.
source: Model refinement calculations were executed using REFMAC (Murshudov et al., 2011), and model building was performed using COOT (Emsley and Cowtan, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Model building was performed using COOT.
source: Model refinement calculations were executed using REFMAC (Murshudov et al., 2011), and model building was performed using COOT (Emsley and Cowtan, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: CDV-H was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip using the direct amine coupling method.
source: CDV-H was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) using the direct amine coupling method.
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: HS-AFM images of CDV-H were acquired in the tapping mode at room temperature.
source: HS-AFM images of CDV-H were acquired in the tapping mode at room temperature using an HS-AFM instrument, NanoExplorer (Research Institute of Biomolecule Metrology).
evidence: This is stated in the materials and methods section.

claim: Images of 200 × 200 pixels from a 100 × 100 nm area were obtained at a scan rate of two frames per second (fps).
source: Images of 200 × 200 pixels from a 100 × 100 nm area were obtained at a scan rate of two frames per second (fps).
